ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In 1831, Faraday demonstrated at a meeting the disk generator he invented (Figure A). It was made using the principle of electromagnetic induction and was the first generator in human history. Figure B is a schematic diagram of this disk generator: the copper disk is mounted on a horizontal copper shaft, and its edge is exactly between the two magnetic poles; two copper pieces C and D are respectively in good contact with the rotating shaft and the edge of the copper disk. When the copper disk is made to rotate, current passes through the resistor R. If the applied magnetic field is a uniform magnetic field, the total resistance of the circuit is constant, and viewed from left to right, the copper disk rotates uniformly in the clockwise direction, and the CRD plane is perpendicular to the plane of the copper disk, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Keep the copper disk stationary, and the magnetic field changes into an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk; then current is generated in the copper disk

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Keep the copper disk stationary. If the magnetic field changes into an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk, what phenomenon will occur in the copper disk?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Keep the copper disk stationary, and the magnetic field changes into an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk; then current is generated in the copper disk
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A shows the physical apparatus of Faraday's disk generator; Figure B is a schematic diagram, with a vertically placed copper disk on the right side, a contact point C marked near the disk surface, and a contact point D marked near the edge of the copper disk; in the external circuit on the left side, a resistor R is connected, and wires connect R with the contact points at C and D to form a loop; multiple horizontal arrows in the figure pass through the copper disk, indicating that the magnetic field lines pass perpendicularly through the disk surface of the copper disk. Reasoning: The problem statement requires “keeping the copper disk stationary,” so it no longer relies on the copper disk cutting magnetic induction lines to generate motional electromotive force; but the magnetic field is changed to “an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk,” and the magnetic flux passing through the disk surface of the copper disk changes with time. According to the law of electromagnetic induction, the changing magnetic flux will produce an induced electromotive force within the copper disk, thereby forming an induced current, which can usually be called an eddy current. Therefore, current will be generated in the copper disk.
